svg.title: Hudi file writers and readers on master (62bae026)
svg.text: Hudi file writers and readers on master (62bae026)

One column per engine. Read top to bottom: the row type, the factory that picks a writer or reader, what each format is written and read with, and how merging works. Gaps and per-record Avro conversions are called out.
picks a factory by HoodieRecordType (AVRO / SPARK / FLINK); each factory switches on HoodieFileFormat; unsupported combinations throw at runtime

g.text: Vortex: Spark only. ORC, HFile: Avro

Avro data block (default inline log block, write version < 10): each Spark or Flink row is converted to Avro (getAvroBytes); read back as Avro, then RecordContext.convertAvroRecord converts each record again.
HFile data block: toIndexedRecord per record. Parquet data block: engine stream writers, no Avro.
Native (v2) log files, write version >= 10: base-format files through the factory, no Avro step.

svg.text: Format support is a matrix with holes: ORC and HFile are written only through the Avro path; Lance is
Spark and Flink only; Vortex is Spark only; Hive and Trino are read-only.
Three Parquet write paths, each deriving its own MessageType (HoodieRowParquetWriteSupport, Flink
ParquetRowDataWriter, parquet-avro), and two Arrow writers for Lance.
Per-record Avro conversion remains on hot paths: Spark's default AVRO record type (rows become Avro
before any writer), Avro and HFile log blocks, payload / custom merging, Trino MOR merging, Hive reads, ORC.
Factories are keyed by record type x file format: a new format needs one factory method per engine, a
new engine needs one per format, and every gap is a runtime exception.
Readers differ in kind: Spark vectorized batches, Flink vectorized readers copied six times, Trino Pages,
Hive row InputFormats, Avro row readers. A shared abstraction has to keep the batch paths.
Native (v2) log files (write version >= 10, the default) write base-format files through the factory;
with the SPARK or FLINK record type there is no Avro step. The direction RFC-88 wants, for one path.
